title: Cloudflare plans to issue quantum-safe TLS certificates
gist: Cloudflare plans to issue free hybrid classic/post-quantum TLS certificates using Merkle Tree Certificates, acquiring a trusted root from GlobalSign, with issuance expected from Q1 2027. Merkle Trees, proposed by Google, keep handshake data near 40KB versus the ~40x blowup of naive post-quantum X.509, and couple transparency logging with issuance.

insights.claim: Cloudflare plans to become one of the first authorities to issue quantum-resistant TLS certificates, offering hybrid classic and Merkle Tree Certificates free to paying and non-paying users.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Positions Cloudflare as a leader in post-quantum web security, potentially pressuring commercial certificate authorities.

insights.claim: Cloudflare will acquire an already trusted certificate root from GlobalSign so millions of websites can enable post-quantum certificates at the flip of a switch without performance overhead.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Buying trusted roots accelerates Cloudflare's entry into the certificate authority market.

insights.claim: Cloudflare is not yet issuing certificates and expects to start in the first quarter of 2027.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Timeline for a commercially available post-quantum WebPKI product.
insights.quote: “We are not issuing certificates yet, and it will be a little while before we do,”

insights.claim: Quantum-proof versions of classical X.509 certificates would add roughly 40 times the data in a TLS handshake, and the added computation and bandwidth would break the Internet as we know it.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Post-quantum migration requires architectural change, not simple algorithm swaps, implying a multi-year transition.
insights.quote: The added computation and bandwidth required to implement such a system would break the Internet as we know it.
insights.locator: Safeguarding the WebPKI against quantum attacks

insights.claim: Google's Merkle Tree design, tested with Cloudflare in pilots, cuts handshake data to about 40 kilobytes, roughly today's level, by having CAs sign a single tree head representing millions of certificates.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A viable scaling path makes post-quantum web encryption deployable.
insights.locator: In February, Google announced a solution

insights.claim: Once viable, Shor’s algorithm could forge classical signatures and certificate log keys, allowing attackers to forge signed certificate timestamps.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Quantum computing poses a direct threat to the trust layer of internet commerce.

insights.claim: The WebPKI overhaul will take years because it requires work from engineers across operating systems, browsers, certificate authorities and Internet infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Post-quantum readiness is a long-duration spending theme for security and infrastructure vendors.

insights.claim: Merkle Tree Certificates make transparency logging a core part of issuance rather than a separate add-on.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Improves resistance to rogue certificates, a key security benefit.
insights.quote: “By coupling issuance and logging, transparency becomes a requirement for operation, rather than an add-on,”

insights.claim: Certificate transparency logs were introduced after the 2011 DigiNotar hack, which minted 500 counterfeit certificates for Google and others, some used to spy on users in Iran.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Historical precedent for the systemic risk of compromised certificate authorities.
